subject: invention/qhapaq-nan
prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Redraw the attached Inca road sketch as a new 3:2 landscape field-sketchbook page. The attachment is ONLY a reference for ink/watercolour style, cream paper, Andean scenery and period clothing. CHANGE the camera and bridge composition completely to make the spatial relationships unambiguous. Camera stands at the entrance of the bridge, slightly above and just to the left of the centre of its walking deck, looking ALONG the bridge toward the far stone anchorage. A continuous narrow woven-grass deck runs from the bottom centre foreground into the upper middle distance, gently sagging between stone abutments over a deep rocky gorge. There are exactly TWO handrails, one on EACH SIDE of the walkway, supported by vertical fibre ropes reaching down to the two deck edges. The bridge has visible walkable WIDTH between these parallel sides, not a single tightrope. One modest-sized Inca traveller is seen from behind walking AWAY from the camera down the CENTRE of this deck. His entire body is INSIDE the two railings: left rail entirely left of his body, right rail entirely right of his body. One sandalled foot is clearly planted flat on the woven deck at its centre, the other just stepping forward immediately above the same deck. Both legs have natural proportions; believable weight and contact shadow. His right hand rests naturally on the right handrail. No railing crosses behind his torso in a way that places him outside the bridge. No standing on an edge rope, no floating body, no feet dangling into the gorge, no person glued to the outside of the near railing. Make him about one-sixth the image height and show enough deck around his feet to judge contact. Plain woven tunic, modest shoulder pack. The deck leads smoothly onto a stone path at the far bank. Broad Andean mountain landscape, sparse terraces, soft pale blue mountains; no other foreground figures. Historically plausible around1500CE, braided plant-fibre cables, no steel, planks or European bridge towers. Preserve the established loose graphite and sepia pen hatching with restrained ochre, grey-green and blue watercolour, irregular unfinished edges dissolving into cream paper. No text, labels, borders, signature or watermarks.
revision_note: Camera moved along the deck so the traveller is clearly inside both railings, with weight supported by the walking surface.
